formulas.name: Static axle loads
formulas.formula: F_f = m · g · b / L,  F_r = m · g · a / L
formulas.where: F_f, F_r front and rear axle loads (N), m mass (kg), g = 9.81 m/s², a distance front axle to CoG (m), b distance CoG to rear axle (m), L = a + b wheelbase (m)
formulas.tip: Front weight fraction = b / L.

formulas.name: Longitudinal weight transfer
formulas.formula: ΔF_z = m · a_x · h / L
formulas.where: ΔF_z load moved between axles (N), m mass (kg), a_x longitudinal acceleration (m/s²), h CoG height (m), L wheelbase (m)
formulas.tip: Braking moves load to the front axle, accelerating to the rear. Divide by g to express it in kg.

formulas.name: Lateral weight transfer
formulas.formula: ΔF_z = m · a_y · h / t
formulas.where: ΔF_z load moved from inner to outer wheels (N), m mass (kg), a_y lateral acceleration (m/s²), h CoG height (m), t track width (m)
formulas.tip: This is the total for the car; the front/rear split depends on roll stiffness distribution.

formulas.name: Lateral acceleration
formulas.formula: a_y = v² / R
formulas.where: a_y lateral acceleration (m/s²), v speed (m/s), R corner radius (m)

formulas.name: Grip-limited cornering speed
formulas.formula: v_max = √(μ · g · R)
formulas.where: v_max maximum speed (m/s), μ tyre–road friction coefficient (–), g = 9.81 m/s², R corner radius (m)
formulas.tip: Flat road and no downforce, so a_y,max = μ · g.

formulas.name: Skidpad lap time
formulas.where: t time for one lap (s), R radius of the driven line (m), a_y lateral acceleration (m/s²; for n g use n · 9.81)
formulas.tip: FS skidpad: 15.25 m inner diameter and a 3 m wide lane, so the lane centreline radius is about 9.1 m. Check the current rules and which radius the question uses.

formulas.name: Friction force
formulas.formula: F = μ · N
formulas.where: F maximum friction force (N), μ friction coefficient (–), N normal load (N)

formulas.name: Braking distance
formulas.formula: s = v² / (2 · a),  a_max = μ · g
formulas.where: s distance to stop (m), v initial speed (m/s), a constant deceleration (m/s²), μ friction coefficient (–), g = 9.81 m/s²
formulas.tip: With a reaction time t_r, add v · t_r.

formulas.name: Understeer gradient
formulas.formula: δ = L / R + K · a_y,  K = W_f / C_αf − W_r / C_αr
formulas.where: δ front wheel steer angle (rad), L wheelbase (m), R corner radius (m), a_y lateral acceleration (g), K understeer gradient (rad/g), W_f, W_r front and rear axle loads (N), C_αf, C_αr front and rear axle cornering stiffness (N/rad)
formulas.tip: K > 0 understeer, K = 0 neutral steer, K < 0 oversteer.

formulas.name: Drag force
formulas.formula: F_D = ½ · ρ · v² · C_D · A
formulas.where: F_D drag (N), ρ air density (kg/m³), v airspeed (m/s), C_D drag coefficient (–), A reference (frontal) area (m²)
formulas.tip: Teams often quote the product C_D · A (m²) directly.

formulas.name: Downforce
formulas.formula: F_L = ½ · ρ · v² · C_L · A
formulas.where: F_L downforce (N), ρ air density (kg/m³), v airspeed (m/s), C_L downforce (negative lift) coefficient magnitude (–), A reference area (m²)
formulas.tip: C_L · A is often given directly; then you do not need A separately.

formulas.name: Dynamic pressure
formulas.formula: q = ½ · ρ · v²
formulas.where: q dynamic pressure (Pa), ρ air density (kg/m³), v airspeed (m/s)
formulas.tip: Any aero force is F = q · C · A.

formulas.name: Power to overcome drag
formulas.formula: P = F_D · v = ½ · ρ · v³ · C_D · A
formulas.where: P power (W), F_D drag (N), v speed (m/s), ρ air density (kg/m³), C_D drag coefficient (–), A reference area (m²)
formulas.tip: Power grows with v³: twice the speed needs eight times the power.

formulas.name: Air density
formulas.formula: ρ = p / (R_s · T)
formulas.where: ρ density (kg/m³), p absolute pressure (Pa), R_s = 287.05 J/(kg·K) for dry air, T temperature (K = °C + 273.15)
formulas.tip: Standard sea-level value: ρ ≈ 1.225 kg/m³ at 15 °C and 101 325 Pa.

formulas.name: Aero balance
formulas.formula: Balance_front = F_L,f / (F_L,f + F_L,r) · 100 %
formulas.where: F_L,f, F_L,r downforce acting on the front and rear axle (N)
formulas.tip: Compare it with the static front weight fraction: a more forward aero balance tends towards oversteer at high speed.

formulas.name: Lift-to-drag ratio
formulas.formula: L/D = C_L / C_D = F_L / F_D
formulas.where: C_L downforce coefficient (–), C_D drag coefficient (–), F_L downforce (N), F_D drag (N)

formulas.name: Cornering speed with downforce
formulas.formula: v = √(μ · m · g / (m / R − ½ · ρ · μ · C_L · A))
formulas.where: v maximum cornering speed (m/s), μ friction coefficient (–), m mass (kg), g = 9.81 m/s², R corner radius (m), ρ air density (kg/m³), C_L · A downforce area (m²)
formulas.tip: From μ · (m · g + F_L) = m · v² / R. If the denominator is zero or negative, grip is not the limiting factor in this simple model.

formulas.name: Normal stress
formulas.formula: σ = F / A
formulas.where: σ stress (Pa), F axial force (N), A cross-section area (m²)
formulas.tip: 1 MPa = 1 N/mm², so working in N and mm gives MPa directly.

formulas.name: Hooke's law and elongation
formulas.formula: σ = E · ε,  ε = ΔL / L₀,  ΔL = F · L₀ / (E · A)
formulas.where: σ stress (Pa), E Young's modulus (Pa), ε strain (–), L₀ original length (m), ΔL elongation (m), F axial force (N), A area (m²)
formulas.tip: Elastic range only. Steel E ≈ 200–210 GPa, aluminium ≈ 70 GPa.

formulas.name: Centre-loaded simply supported beam
formulas.formula: M_max = F · L / 4,  δ_max = F · L³ / (48 · E · I)
formulas.where: M_max bending moment at mid-span (N·m), F point load at mid-span (N), L span between supports (m), δ_max mid-span deflection (m), E Young's modulus (Pa), I second moment of area (m⁴)

formulas.name: Bending stress
formulas.formula: σ = M · y / I = M / W,  W = I / y_max
formulas.where: σ bending stress (Pa), M bending moment (N·m), y distance from the neutral axis (m), I second moment of area (m⁴), W section modulus (m³), y_max distance to the outer fibre (m)
formulas.tip: The maximum stress is at the outer fibre, y = y_max.

formulas.name: Round tube section
formulas.where: I second moment of area (m⁴), W section modulus (m³), D outer diameter (m), d inner diameter (m) = D − 2 · wall thickness
formulas.tip: Solid bar: set d = 0.

formulas.name: Rectangular tube section
formulas.formula: I = (B · H³ − b · h³) / 12,  W = (B · H³ − b · h³) / (6 · H)
formulas.where: I second moment of area (m⁴), W section modulus (m³), B, H outer width and height (m), b, h inner width and height (m); H is measured in the bending direction
formulas.tip: Height counts cubed, so turning a tube on its side changes its stiffness a lot.

formulas.name: Euler buckling load
formulas.formula: F_cr = π² · E · I / (K · L)²
formulas.where: F_cr critical load (N), E Young's modulus (Pa), I smallest second moment of area (m⁴), L column length (m), K effective length factor: 1 pinned–pinned, 0.5 fixed–fixed, ≈ 0.7 fixed–pinned, 2 fixed–free
formulas.tip: Valid for slender columns that fail by buckling before yielding.

formulas.name: Impact energy and deceleration
formulas.formula: E = ½ · m · v²,  a_avg = v² / (2 · s),  F_avg = E / s,  n = a_avg / g
formulas.where: E kinetic energy (J), m mass (kg), v impact speed (m/s), s stopping (crush) distance (m), a_avg average deceleration (m/s²), F_avg average force (N), n deceleration in g, g = 9.81 m/s²
formulas.tip: FS impact attenuator reference case: 300 kg at 7 m/s gives 7350 J, with at most 20 g average and 40 g peak. Check the current rules.

formulas.name: Safety factor
formulas.formula: SF = σ_allow / σ_actual
formulas.where: SF safety factor (–), σ_allow material strength used as the limit, usually yield (Pa), σ_actual calculated stress (Pa)
formulas.tip: For buckling use F_cr / F. Check whether the question uses yield or ultimate strength.

formulas.name: Power from torque
formulas.formula: P = T · ω
formulas.where: P power (W), T torque (N·m), ω angular speed (rad/s)

formulas.name: rpm to rad/s
formulas.where: ω angular speed (rad/s), n rotational speed (rpm)
formulas.tip: Shortcut: P (kW) = T (N·m) · n (rpm) / 9549.

formulas.name: Gear ratio and wheel torque
formulas.formula: i = n_in / n_out = z_out / z_in,  T_wheel = T_motor · i · η
formulas.where: i gear ratio (–), n_in, n_out input and output speeds (rpm), z_in, z_out teeth on input and output gears (–), T_wheel, T_motor torques (N·m), η transmission efficiency (–)
formulas.tip: Torque goes up by i and speed goes down by i; power stays the same apart from losses.

formulas.name: Tractive force
formulas.formula: F_x = T_wheel / r
formulas.where: F_x tractive force at the ground (N), T_wheel total torque at the driven wheels (N·m), r loaded tyre radius (m)
formulas.tip: It cannot exceed μ times the load on the driven wheels.

formulas.name: Acceleration and 0–100 km/h
formulas.formula: a = F_net / m,  t = Δv / a,  s = ½ · a · t²
formulas.where: a acceleration (m/s²), F_net tractive force minus resistances (N), m mass including driver (kg), t time (s), Δv speed change (m/s; 100 km/h = 27.78 m/s), s distance from standstill (m)
formulas.tip: Assumes constant acceleration. Time to cover a distance from rest: t = √(2 · s / a).

formulas.name: Vehicle speed from motor speed
formulas.formula: v = 2π · r · n_motor / (60 · i)
formulas.where: v vehicle speed (m/s), r tyre radius (m), n_motor motor speed (rpm), i overall gear ratio (–)

formulas.name: Efficiency and energy
formulas.formula: η = P_out / P_in,  η_total = η₁ · η₂ · …,  E = P · t
formulas.where: η efficiency (–), P_out, P_in output and input power (W), η₁, η₂ efficiencies of each stage (–), E energy (J), P average power (W), t time (s)
formulas.tip: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ.

formulas.name: Rolling resistance and road load
formulas.formula: F_rr = C_rr · m · g,  P = (F_rr + F_D) · v
formulas.where: F_rr rolling resistance (N), C_rr rolling resistance coefficient (–), m mass (kg), g = 9.81 m/s², P power needed at constant speed (W), F_D aerodynamic drag (N), v speed (m/s)
formulas.tip: C_rr is roughly 0.01–0.015 for car tyres on asphalt or concrete.

formulas.name: Compression ratio
formulas.formula: CR = (V_d + V_c) / V_c,  V_d = π · B² · S / 4
formulas.where: CR compression ratio (–), V_d swept volume of one cylinder (m³), V_c clearance volume (m³), B bore (m), S stroke (m)

formulas.name: Pack voltage (cells in series)
formulas.formula: V_pack = n_s · V_cell
formulas.where: V_pack pack voltage (V), n_s number of cells in series (–), V_cell cell voltage (V)
formulas.tip: Use the maximum cell voltage (often 4.2 V for Li-ion) for maximum TS voltage and the nominal voltage (≈ 3.6–3.7 V) for energy.

formulas.name: Pack capacity and energy
formulas.formula: C_pack = n_p · C_cell,  E = n_s · n_p · V_cell,nom · C_cell
formulas.where: C_pack, C_cell pack and cell capacity (Ah), n_p cells in parallel (–), n_s cells in series (–), V_cell,nom nominal cell voltage (V), E energy (Wh)
formulas.tip: A 140s4p pack has n_s = 140 and n_p = 4. Divide Wh by 1000 for kWh, multiply by 3600 for J.

formulas.name: Current from power
formulas.formula: I = P / V
formulas.where: I current (A), P power (W), V voltage (V)
formulas.tip: 80 kW at 400 V is 200 A. The 80 kW limit at the accumulator outlet comes from recent FS rules; check the current rules.

formulas.name: Resistive losses and voltage sag
formulas.formula: P_loss = I² · R,  V_term = V_oc − I · R,  R_pack = n_s · R_cell / n_p
formulas.where: P_loss heat generated (W), I current (A), R resistance (Ω), V_term terminal voltage under load (V), V_oc open-circuit voltage (V), R_cell internal resistance of one cell (Ω)
formulas.tip: R_pack ignores busbars and connectors; add them in series if given.

formulas.name: Precharge (RC charging)
formulas.formula: V_C(t) = V_TS · (1 − e^(−t/τ)),  τ = R · C,  t_x = −τ · ln(1 − x)
formulas.where: V_C voltage on the vehicle side (V), V_TS accumulator voltage (V), t time (s), τ time constant (s), R precharge resistance (Ω), C DC-link capacitance (F), x target fraction (e.g. 0.95)
formulas.tip: 90 % takes ≈ 2.3 τ and 95 % ≈ 3 τ. FS Rules 2026 ask for at least 95 % before the second AIR closes (older rulebooks said 90 %); check the current rules.

formulas.name: Discharge (RC decay)
formulas.formula: V(t) = V₀ · e^(−t/τ),  t = τ · ln(V₀ / V_safe)
formulas.where: V voltage (V), V₀ starting voltage (V), τ = R · C discharge time constant (s), V_safe target voltage (V)
formulas.tip: Recent FS rules require the TS to fall below 60 V DC within 5 s after shutdown; check the current rules.

formulas.name: IMD response value
formulas.formula: R_min = 500 Ω/V · V_TS,max
formulas.where: R_min insulation resistance at which the IMD must trip (Ω), V_TS,max maximum TS voltage (V)
formulas.tip: Example: 600 V gives 300 kΩ. The 500 Ω/V value is from recent FS rules; check the current rules.

formulas.name: Fuse sizing basics
formulas.formula: I_load ≤ I_rated ≤ I_conductor,  I_interrupt > I_sc ≈ V_pack / R_loop
formulas.where: I_load continuous load current (A), I_rated fuse continuous rating (A), I_conductor current rating of the protected wire or busbar (A), I_interrupt fuse breaking capacity (A), I_sc short-circuit current (A), R_loop total resistance of the fault loop, including cell internal resistance (Ω)
formulas.tip: The fuse voltage rating must also be at least the maximum TS voltage.

formulas.name: Energy meter
formulas.formula: P = V · I,  E = Σ V · I · Δt
formulas.where: P instantaneous power (W), V TS voltage (V), I TS current (A), E energy (J), Δt sample interval (s)
formulas.tip: The officials' meter (called data logger in recent FS rules) records TS voltage and current to check the power limit and score efficiency; check the current rules.

formulas.name: Ohm's law and power
formulas.formula: V = I · R,  P = V · I = I² · R = V² / R
formulas.where: V voltage (V), I current (A), R resistance (Ω), P power dissipated (W)
formulas.tip: Check that each resistor's power rating exceeds P.

formulas.name: Series and parallel resistors
formulas.formula: R_s = R₁ + R₂ + …,  1 / R_p = 1 / R₁ + 1 / R₂ + …
formulas.where: R_s series equivalent (Ω), R_p parallel equivalent (Ω), R₁, R₂ individual resistors (Ω)
formulas.tip: Two in parallel: R₁ · R₂ / (R₁ + R₂). Capacitors combine the other way round.

formulas.name: Voltage divider
formulas.formula: V_out = V_in · R₂ / (R₁ + R₂)
formulas.where: V_out output across R₂ (V), V_in input voltage (V), R₁ top resistor (Ω), R₂ bottom resistor (Ω)
formulas.tip: Valid without load; a load in parallel with R₂ lowers V_out.

formulas.name: RC and RL time constants
formulas.formula: τ_RC = R · C,  τ_RL = L / R,  v(t) = V · (1 − e^(−t/τ))
formulas.where: τ time constant (s), R resistance (Ω), C capacitance (F), L inductance (H), v(t) capacitor voltage while charging (V), V final voltage (V)

formulas.name: Rise time (10–90 %)
formulas.where: t_r rise time (s), τ = R · C (s), f_c −3 dB cut-off frequency (Hz)

formulas.name: Capacitor energy and charge
formulas.formula: E = ½ · C · V²,  Q = C · V
formulas.where: E stored energy (J), C capacitance (F), V voltage (V), Q charge (C)

formulas.name: ADC resolution
formulas.formula: LSB = V_ref / 2ⁿ,  code ≈ V_in / LSB
formulas.where: LSB voltage step (V), V_ref reference voltage (V), n number of bits (–), code output value (rounded down, at most 2ⁿ − 1), V_in input voltage (V)
formulas.tip: Some sources use V_ref / (2ⁿ − 1); check which convention the question expects.

formulas.name: CAN bit timing
formulas.formula: t_bit = 1 / bitrate = (1 + TSEG1 + TSEG2) · t_q,  t_q = BRP / f_clk,  SP = (1 + TSEG1) / (1 + TSEG1 + TSEG2)
formulas.where: t_bit bit time (s), t_q time quantum (s), TSEG1 propagation plus phase segment 1 (in t_q), TSEG2 phase segment 2 (in t_q), BRP baud-rate prescaler (–), f_clk CAN clock (Hz), SP sample point (fraction of the bit)
formulas.tip: The 1 is the sync segment. Sample points around 75–87.5 % are common for classic CAN.

formulas.name: Plausibility checks (rules of thumb)
formulas.formula: APPS: |p₁ − p₂| > 10 %-points for > 100 ms → cut motor power;  BSPD: hard braking while P ≥ 5 kW for > 500 ms → open the SDC
formulas.where: p₁, p₂ pedal travel read by the two APPS (%), P power delivered to the motors (W), SDC shutdown circuit
formulas.tip: The SDC is a series loop of safety switches; opening any one opens the AIRs. Thresholds are from recent FS rules; check the current rules.

formulas.name: AS states
formulas.formula: AS Off → AS Ready → AS Driving → AS Finished;  EBS activated unexpectedly → AS Emergency
formulas.where: Off: default state. Ready: mission selected, ASMS on, brake checks passed, TS active and brakes engaged. Driving: ready-to-drive after the RES Go signal (at least 5 s in Ready). Finished: EBS activated after the mission is completed and the car is at standstill. Emergency: EBS activated in any other case, or the RES opened the SDC.
formulas.tip: ASSI lights: Off none, Ready yellow steady, Driving yellow flashing, Emergency blue flashing, Finished blue steady. Check the current rules.

formulas.name: Stopping distance
formulas.formula: s = v · t_d + v² / (2 · a)
formulas.where: s total stopping distance (m), v initial speed (m/s), t_d delay before deceleration starts (s), a average deceleration (m/s²)
formulas.tip: The EBS must be passive (stored mechanical energy), so losing power brakes the car. Recent FS rules: ≤ 200 ms reaction and > 10 m/s² average deceleration in the dry; check the current rules.

formulas.name: Stopping time
formulas.formula: t_stop = t_d + v / a
formulas.where: t_stop time to standstill (s), t_d delay (s), v initial speed (m/s), a average deceleration (m/s²)

formulas.name: Required deceleration
formulas.where: a deceleration needed (m/s²), v initial speed (m/s), s available distance (m), t_d delay (s)

formulas.name: Lidar range (time of flight)
formulas.formula: d = c · Δt / 2
formulas.where: d distance to target (m), c = 3.0 · 10⁸ m/s speed of light, Δt round-trip time (s)

formulas.name: Lidar point spacing
formulas.formula: Δs ≈ d · Δθ,  n ≈ w / (d · Δθ)
formulas.where: Δs gap between neighbouring points (m), d range (m), Δθ angular resolution (rad; deg · π / 180), n points across an object, w object width or height (m)
formulas.tip: Vertical resolution usually limits how many rings hit a small cone far away.

formulas.name: Pinhole camera size
formulas.formula: w_px = f_px · W / Z
formulas.where: w_px object size in the image (px), f_px focal length in pixels (px), W real object size (m), Z distance along the optical axis (m)

formulas.name: DV missions
formulas.formula: Acceleration: 75 m straight · Skidpad: figure of eight · Autocross: one lap, track unknown · Trackdrive: 10 laps, then stop
formulas.where: The mission is selected on the car before staging; each run must end with the car stopped in AS Finished.
formulas.tip: Distances and lap counts are from recent FS rules; check the current rules and the event handbook.

formulas.name: Dynamic score (FS Rules 2026)
formulas.formula: Score = (P_max − P_min) · ((T_max − T_team) / (T_max − T_min))² + P_min
formulas.where: P_max maximum points for the discipline, P_min minimum points for a valid run, T_team team's best time including penalties (capped at T_max) (s), T_min fastest time including penalties (s), T_max time limit for the discipline (s)
formulas.tip: Rulebooks before 2026 used ratio forms such as (T_max / T_team − 1) / (T_max / T_min − 1). Answer old quiz questions with that year's rules.

formulas.name: T_max and P_min per discipline
formulas.formula: Skidpad 1.35 · T_min, 0.05 · P_max;  Acceleration 1.7 · T_min, 0.05 · P_max;  Autocross 1.4 · T_min, 0.1 · P_max;  Endurance 1.5 · T_min, 0.1 · P_max
formulas.where: T_min fastest time including penalties (s), P_max maximum points for the discipline
formulas.tip: Values from FS Rules 2026; check the current rules.

formulas.name: DV skidpad and acceleration (ranking)
formulas.formula: Score = P_max · (N_all + 1 − R) / N_all
formulas.where: P_max maximum points, R the team's rank on best autonomous time including penalties, N_all number of teams with at least one valid manual or autonomous run
formulas.tip: Only the ranking matters, not the time gap. FS Rules 2026; check the current rules.

formulas.name: Trackdrive (Driverless Cup)
formulas.formula: Score = 0.75 · P_max · (T_max / T_team − 1) + 0.025 · P_max · laps
formulas.where: P_max maximum points, T_team corrected elapsed time (s, capped at T_max), T_max = 2 · fastest corrected time (s), laps completed laps
formulas.tip: Ten laps give the full 25 % lap bonus. FS Rules 2026; check the current rules.

formulas.name: Efficiency
formulas.formula: EF = T² · E,  Score = P_max · ((EF_max − EF_team) / (EF_max − EF_min))²,  EF_max = 2 · EF_min
formulas.where: EF efficiency factor, T uncorrected endurance driving time (s), E energy used (EV) or corrected fuel mass (CV), EF_min lowest EF of all eligible teams
formulas.tip: Use consistent units for all teams. FS Rules 2026; check the current rules.

formulas.name: Skidpad run time
formulas.formula: T = (T_left + T_right) / 2 + penalties
formulas.where: T run time (s), T_left, T_right timed lap on the left and right circle (s)

formulas.name: Corrected time with penalties
formulas.formula: T_corr = T_raw + n_DOO · t_DOO + n_OC · t_OC
formulas.where: T_raw measured time (s), n_DOO cones down or out, t_DOO penalty per cone (s), n_OC off-course events, t_OC penalty per off-course (s)
formulas.tip: FS Rules 2026: DOO 2 s (0.2 s in skidpad), OC 10 s in autocross, endurance and trackdrive, disqualification in acceleration and skidpad. Check the current rules and event handbook.

formulas.name: Points split
formulas.formula: Statics 325 + Dynamics 675 = 1000;  Driverless Cup 600
formulas.where: Statics: Business Plan 75, Cost and Manufacturing 100, Engineering Design 150. Dynamics: Acceleration 50, DV Acceleration 75, Skidpad 50, DV Skidpad 75, Autocross 100, Endurance 250, Efficiency 75. Driverless Cup: Engineering Design 150, DV Acceleration 75, DV Skidpad 75, DV Autocross 100, Trackdrive 200.
formulas.tip: FS Rules 2026 split; events can change it, so check the current rules and event handbook.

formulas.name: Speed units
formulas.where: v speed; multiply m/s by 3.6 to get km/h

formulas.name: Acceleration in g
formulas.formula: n = a / g,  g = 9.81 m/s²
formulas.where: n acceleration in g (–), a acceleration (m/s²), g standard gravity (9.80665 m/s² exactly)
formulas.tip: Use the value of g the question gives; answers can differ slightly between 9.81 and 9.8.

formulas.name: Energy units
formulas.formula: 1 kWh = 3.6 · 10⁶ J,  1 Wh = 3600 J,  E (Wh) = V · C (Ah)
formulas.where: E energy, V voltage (V), C charge capacity (Ah)

formulas.name: Angles and rotation
formulas.formula: θ (rad) = θ (°) · π / 180,  ω (rad/s) = 2π · n (rpm) / 60
formulas.where: θ angle, ω angular speed, n rotational speed (rpm)

formulas.name: Rounding and units
formulas.formula: Keep ≥ 4 significant figures while calculating; round only the final answer
formulas.where: Answer in the unit and precision the question asks for (e.g. kW, not W; two decimals if requested)
formulas.tip: Read the question for the unit asked and whether it wants a rounded or truncated value.
